Recommendation: Once FIDO2 is enabled (see AUTH004), scope registration to an approved AAGUID allow-list via key restrictions rather than accepting any FIDO2 authenticator. Two documented caveats. First, AAGUID restrictions suppress the registration campaign nudge for affected users (see RCAMP001), and a tenant targeting specific AAGUIDs does not get the automatic switch to passkey targeting under 'Microsoft managed' state - so this and an active campaign can quietly work against each other. Second, Microsoft is explicit that key restrictions are only advisory unless attestation is also enforced: 'Use AAGUID lists as a policy guide rather than a strict security control when Enforce attestation is set to No.' An allow-list without PASS001 is a guardrail, not a control. Note also that removing a previously allowed AAGUID immediately stops existing registrations of that model from being usable for sign-in. Graph only returns the raw AAGUIDs on that list, not vendor/model names - see the 'FIDO2 Key Restrictions' section (Policy Inventory tab) for those AAGUIDs resolved to readable key names where recognized.
